items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: why is of course back to George Martin’s skill as a producer

ctx.x: Was there any noise — no pun intended — from the musicians’ union about the rise of synthesizers in the studio?

Yeah there was a lot. The union, their focus has always been within — their boundaries are defined by things that they understand which traditionally has been Broadway shows, weddings, club dates. And they never really related well to the recording scene. They’re actually better at it now. But by the time they caught up it was too late. I remember in the 70s there was an instrument called the mellotron, which was a keyboard instrument and it was a bear. It was like it was a real beast. And it had, each key was…
It was just its own thing.
